restated_task: Add an instance method `Version.is_compatible(other: 'Version') -> bool` to the Version class in src/semver/version.py. The method returns True when `other` (the new version) can be used in place of `self` (the old version). Compatibility rules: majors must be equal; new.minor >= old.minor; prerelease parts must be equal (both None counts as equal); patch is ignored. Major version 0 is special: only identical versions (major, minor, patch, prerelease all equal) are compatible. If `other` is not a Version instance (subclasses allowed), raise TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got ' followed by the type representation. Add a docstring with at least two doctest examples. Do not modify any other public behavior, tests, docs, or packaging; keep the existing pytest suite passing.

interface_contract.name: Version.is_compatible
interface_contract.behavior: Returns True when `other` (new version) is compatible with `self` (old version). Compatibility rules: 1) major versions must be equal. 2) If major == 0, versions are compatible only if major, minor, patch, and prerelease are all identical (patch and prerelease must match exactly). 3) If major > 0, new.minor >= old.minor and prerelease parts must be equal (both None counts as equal); patch is ignored. Subclasses of Version are accepted as `other`.
error_cases: TypeError: raised when `other` is not an instance of Version (or subclass). Message must start with 'Expected a Version type but got ' followed by the type representation (e.g., "<class 'str'>").

acceptance_criteria: Version(1, 2, 4).is_compatible(Version(1, 2, 3)) is True (patch ignored, minor equal)
Version(0, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(0, 1, 1)) is False (major 0 requires identical patch)
Version(1, 1, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is False (new minor < old minor)
Version(1, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0, 'rc1')) is False (prerelease differs: None vs 'rc1')
Version(1, 0, 0, 'rc1').is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is False (prerelease differs: 'rc1' vs None)
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible('wrongtype') raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got '
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible({'a': 2}) raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got '
Version(1, 2, 3).is_compatible([]) raises TypeError with message starting with 'Expected a Version type but got '
Subclass instance accepted: class CustomVersion(Version): pass; CustomVersion(1, 0, 0).is_compatible(Version(1, 0, 0)) is True
Method docstring contains at least two doctest examples
Existing pytest test suite (tests/) passes without modification
